body: Please add your full system details, this is probably related to your graphics

Which rendering method (Forward+, Mobile, Compatibility) and driver (Vulkan, D3D12, OpenGL) are you using in that project?

Note that 4.6 changes the default rendering driver for Forward+ and Mobile to D3D12 on Windows, while it was Vulkan in 4.5. This shouldn't affect pre-existing projects but if you ran the project upgrade tool, it would switch your project to D3D12 too.

You can change the driver in the project settings to test various options and see if there are some which crash and others which don't.

@Galleom Do you have Steam running when these issues happen? See #115139 for context, the symptoms sound similar and this one was worked around by disabling Steam's Fossilize tool (Vulkan shader pre-caching). It may not at all be the same issue you're having, but it's worth checking.

@akien-mga Hm, yes I did have Steam running in my inital tests since it's one of my startup apps. However, closing steam through "Exit Steam" and changing the renderer back to Vulkan still causes the crash to happen.

Can you try (temporarily) to disable shader pre-caching on Steam?
You can do it by toggling "Allow vulkan shader background processing" in Settings > Shader Pre-caching.

I'm not sure if this is the same issue that I'm having but mine not only crashes Godot but my AMD driver too, it probably corrupted the driver too!. Things got so bad last time that my device manager disabled my GPU and had to reinstall the driver.

@akien-mga had some difficulty finding the setting, if someone else needs help, it's on the "Downloads" tab.

But yeah, it still crashes this way.

Could you try 4.6-rc2 which was just released? It should fix #115139 and may fix your issue too.

It seems like to properly disable Fossilize running on Godot you also need to disable "Enable Shader Pre-Caching" in Steam > Settings > Downloads. But normally 4.6-rc2 should solve this without require a change to the Steam config.

If neither option changes anything for you, then the issue is different and we should explore other clues.

Hello, this sounds somewhat similar to another issue I was looking into deeply yesterday that I was having. 

Here's a link to that issue in case it's helpful in any way: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/101452

The issue, for some people(myself included) were having severe driver crashes sporadically when calling get_tree().quit() to exit the in editor version of a project. Changing the Driver.windows from vulkan to d3d12 seems to fix it. It seems like a vulkan issue on Windows with an Nvidia GPU for the most part(possibly tied to older CPUs as well but that's speculative on my part). There's a full explanation I left on the linked issue for how it was affecting me personally. 

Just wanted to help make sure info was reaching people as needed, hopefully this helps. I like Godot and wanna see it grow and improve.

Also having crashes in 4.6 since dev-1, but only now I found a way to consistently crash Godot with an MRP.

It crashes on Forward+ regardless of D3D12 or Vulkan. On Mobile is hit or miss. Doesn't crash on Compatibility.

**Reproducible on**: 4.6-dev1 to 4.6-rc1
**Not reproducible on**: 4.5.1 stable

### Steps to reproduce
1) Open the MRP bellow.
1) In the first ReflectionProbe, set "Update Mode" to "Always (Slow)". Set the second to "Once (Fast)".
1) Run the project.
1) Move the camera with "wasd" or arrow keys. The game will crash.

### MRP

[Godot-4.6-ReflectionProbe-Crash.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24807971/Godot-4.6-ReflectionProbe-Crash.zip)

Note that setting the second ReflectionProbe to "Always" will not result in crash, only the first one. Even if you change the order, it only crashes if the first ReflectionProbe **in the tree** is set to "Always" and the second is set to "Once".

I believe that this issue is beyond just the probes themselves since 4.6 have many random crashes since dev1. Hope that this method to reproduce the crash helps to find the real culprit :)
